source_text: Still going?  This is a slow demo.
reply_text:
No, it finished. My last message was the result: all 2,446 constants came back identical. You're right that it's slow, though. The whole run took about 6 minutes:

| step | time |
|---|---|
| start Lean from the generated Python | 56 s |
| elaborate `M3_Pythagoras.lean` (mostly importing `Init`) | 158 s |
| import `Lean.Declaration` so Lean's own types (`Expr`, `ConstantInfo`, …) are available | 112 s |
| generate classes and round-trip 2,446 constants | 46 s |

Only the last 46 s is the typed layer itself. The other ~5½ minutes is Lean starting up and importing modules in Python, which repeats on every run.

The cheap fix is to pay that cost once. `tools/warm_replay.py` already starts Lean once and serves each request from a forked copy. If I extend it to also hold the `Init` and `Lean.Declaration` environments, each demo request would take well under a minute, most of it the round trip. I'd do that before the "Python → Lean" demo, since that one gets run interactively and repeatedly.

The deeper speed-up is the "faster generated code" item on the issue #5 list, which is a bigger job.

I can make the warm server next unless you'd rather I start on writing a statement in Python and having the kernel check it.
